title: [ROCm] Fix Python 3.15 manywheel build: resolve numpy source build against target Python
body:
## Summary

The nightly **ROCm** `py3_15` / `py3_15t` manywheel binary builds fail in `.ci/manywheel/build_install_deps.py` while building **numpy from source** (Python 3.15 has no numpy wheels on any index yet, so a source build is unavoidable). numpy's meson build resolves its `python3` dependency via **pkg-config**, and the manylinux ROCm image carries the distro's system `python3-devel` (Python 3.6) on pkg-config's default search path:

```
Determining dependency 'python3' with pkg-config
`pkg-config --cflags python3` -> -I/usr/include/python3.6m
`pkg-config --libs   python3` -> -L/usr/lib64 -lpython3.6m
Run-time dependency python3 found: YES 3.6
sanity_check_for_cython.c:23:6: error: #error Cython requires Python 3.8+.
```

This runs before the target env is created, so **all** ROCm py3.15 jobs fail identically. The **XPU py3.15 builds pass** — that image has no stray system `python3.pc`, so the same numpy source build resolves the correct interpreter and succeeds (pip `-q` is silent on success, which is why the XPU log shows no numpy build).

## Fixes

1. **`prefer_target_python_pkgconfig()`** — prepend the target interpreter's own `pkgconfig` dir to `PKG_CONFIG_PATH` so `pkg-config python3` resolves the CPython we're building for instead of the image's system 3.6 (pkg-config searches `PKG_CONFIG_PATH` before its default libdir). The same guard is added to `build_common.sh`.
2. **`numpy_pin()` bug** — `"cp315".startswith("cp31")` is `True`, so 3.15 was wrongly bucketed to `numpy==2.1.0`, which predates 3.15 and cannot build for it. Switched to numeric `(major, minor)` comparison and added a `cp315 -> 2.5.1` pin (2.5.1 builds on 3.15). Mirrored in `build_common.sh`'s `case`.

## Test plan

- Re-run the ROCm `manywheel-py3_15-rocm*` / `py3_15t-rocm*` binary builds; the numpy source build should resolve `/opt/python/cp315-cp315` and compile.
- Existing Pythons are unaffected: the pkg-config prepend is a no-op where the correct `python3.pc` already resolves, and `numpy_pin()` returns the same values for 3.10–3.14 as before (3.13 -> 2.1.0, 3.14 -> 2.3.4).
